description: Procedural Skills Approval Panel -- review interface for auto-extracted fix patterns learned from successful workflow runs. When a workflow iterates 3+ times and produces an effective fix (reuse_count >= 2), the fix pattern is captured as a reusable skill with source='auto' and approval_status='pending'. Users review pending skills here and approve or reject them; approved skills are injected into future worker agent prompts during the agentic phase (up to 10 skills, 2000-char token budget). The self-repair loop auto-disables approved skills that cause 3+ consecutive verification failures by reverting them to 'pending'. Data source: GET /skills fetches from user_skills table (SQLite), filtered client-side to source='auto'. Approval mutations use POST /skills/{id}/approve. Skill metrics available at GET /graph/skill-metrics. Skills are also mirrored to PG observations (topic_key='skill:<slug>') for cross-session full-text search, and materialized as Skill nodes in the knowledge graph with DerivedFrom, UsedIn, and Supersedes edges.

groups.name: Page Purpose and Identity
groups.description: The Skills page is the human review gate for auto-extracted procedural memory. It answers: 'What fix patterns has the system learned, and should they be trusted to guide future work?' The page header identifies itself with a lightning bolt (Zap) icon, the title 'Procedural Skills', and a subtitle explaining provenance. The page is empty by default until workflows extract skills -- this is expected, not an error.

assertions.description: Users see the heading 'Procedural Skills' identifying this as the skill review interface
Users see the subtitle 'Auto-extracted from successful runs' explaining that skills are machine-generated, not manually created

When no pending skills exist (default state for a fresh system), users see guidance text explaining how skills are created: 'No pending skills to review. Skills are auto-extracted when workflows succeed after complex fixes.'
assertions.notes: This message appears on the Pending filter (default). Other filters show 'No {status} skills found.'

groups.name: Page Navigation
groups.description: The Skills page is reachable from the runner sidebar under the OBSERVE navigation group, positioned after Meta-Optimizer. The sidebar entry uses a Zap icon with amber (#F59E0B) color. The tab ID is 'skills' and the page is lazy-loaded via React.lazy.

assertions.description: The sidebar contains a 'Skills' navigation entry that users can click to open this page
After clicking the Skills sidebar entry, the main content area shows the 'Procedural Skills' heading within 2 seconds
assertions.notes: Component is lazy-loaded (React.lazy) so there may be a brief loading flash on first visit.

groups.name: Core UI Elements
groups.description: The page has a header bar (title + subtitle + refresh button), a filter tab bar (4 buttons: Pending, Approved, Rejected, All), and a scrollable content area showing skill rows or empty state. The refresh button shows a spinning icon during API fetch.

assertions.description: A refresh button exists in the header bar with title='Refresh', showing a RefreshCw icon
assertions.notes: The button has no visible text -- only an icon. Find by title attribute or by proximity to the heading.

assertions.description: The 'Pending' filter tab button exists with a count suffix showing (N) where N is the number of pending skills
assertions.expected: Button text is 'Pending (N)' where N is the count of pending auto-skills. When selected, it has class bg-primary text-primary-foreground.

assertions.description: The 'Approved' filter tab button exists with a count suffix
The 'Rejected' filter tab button exists with a count suffix
The 'All' filter tab button exists (shows no count suffix)

groups.name: Skill Row Data Display
groups.description: Each skill is rendered as a row with: a chevron toggle (ChevronRight when collapsed, ChevronDown when expanded), a status icon (green CheckCircle for approved, red XCircle for rejected, amber Clock for pending), the skill name (truncated via CSS text-ellipsis), and secondary metadata line showing 'category . vX.Y.Z . used Nx'. Data comes from GET /skills, filtered client-side to source='auto'.

assertions.description: Each skill row shows a clickable chevron icon that toggles between collapsed (right arrow) and expanded (down arrow) states
assertions.precondition: At least one auto-extracted skill exists in the user_skills table with source='auto'

assertions.description: The skill name is shown as the primary text in the row, using font-medium weight and text-xs size. Auto-extracted skills have names starting with 'Auto:' followed by the fix description
assertions.precondition: At least one auto-extracted skill exists in the user_skills table with source='auto'

assertions.description: Below each skill name, a metadata line shows the category, version (e.g., 'v1.0.0'), and usage count (e.g., 'used 0x') separated by middot characters
assertions.precondition: At least one auto-extracted skill exists in the user_skills table with source='auto'
assertions.expected: Text format is '{category} . v{version} . used {N}x' where N is an integer >= 0

assertions.description: Pending skills show an amber Clock icon as their status indicator
assertions.precondition: At least one skill with approval_status='pending' exists
assertions.expected: The row contains an SVG element with class text-amber-500 (the Clock icon)

groups.name: Expanded Skill Detail View
groups.description: Clicking the chevron expands a detail panel below the skill row, indented to align with the skill name. The panel shows labeled fields: Description (full text), Tags (comma-separated), Phases (comma-separated), and Created (localized datetime). For auto-extracted skills, a Provenance section appears with a muted background showing Fix type (monospace), Source run (monospace, 10px), Fix ID (monospace, 10px), and Effectiveness (green text). Provenance data is parsed from the skill's description field which embeds 'task_run: {id}, fix: {id}' and 'Fix type: {type}' patterns.

assertions.description: The expanded view shows a 'Description:' label followed by the full skill description text
assertions.precondition: A skill row has been expanded by clicking its chevron
assertions.expected: For auto-extracted skills, the description text includes: workflow name, task_run ID, fix ID, fix type, and iteration count

assertions.description: The expanded view shows a 'Tags:' label followed by comma-separated tag values
assertions.precondition: A skill row has been expanded by clicking its chevron
assertions.expected: For auto-extracted skills, tags include 'auto' and the fix type (e.g., 'auto, selector_fix'). Skills with no tags show 'none'.

assertions.description: The expanded view shows a 'Phases:' label followed by comma-separated workflow phase names
assertions.precondition: A skill row has been expanded by clicking its chevron
assertions.expected: Auto-extracted skills show 'agentic' since they are restricted to the agentic phase

assertions.description: The expanded view shows a 'Created:' label followed by a localized datetime string
assertions.precondition: A skill row has been expanded by clicking its chevron

assertions.description: The expanded view shows a 'Provenance' section with a muted background (bg-muted/50) containing fix traceability data
assertions.precondition: An auto-extracted skill with a parseable description (containing 'task_run:' and 'Fix type:' patterns) has been expanded
assertions.expected: Section displays: Fix type (monospace font), Source run ID (monospace, 10px), Fix ID from source_fix_id column (monospace, 10px), Effectiveness rating (green text, typically 'effective')

assertions.description: The provenance section shows 'Fix ID:' followed by the source_fix_id value in monospace font
assertions.precondition: An auto-extracted skill with source_fix_id set has been expanded

groups.name: Approval and Rejection Actions
groups.description: Pending skills show inline Approve (green) and Reject (red) buttons in the row. Approved/rejected skills show these buttons in the expanded detail panel instead, along with a 'Reset to Pending' button (amber). All three buttons call POST /skills/{id}/approve with the target status. The UI updates optimistically -- the skill immediately moves to the new filter tab. If the API returns a non-ok response, the update is not applied (no rollback of optimistic state since the API call happens before the state update).

assertions.description: Users can click 'Approve' on a pending skill to mark it for injection into future worker prompts. The button has green styling (bg-green-500/10 text-green-600).
assertions.precondition: At least one skill with approval_status='pending' exists in user_skills with source='auto'
assertions.expected: After clicking, the skill disappears from the Pending tab. The Pending count decreases by 1 and the Approved count increases by 1. The skill appears under the Approved filter tab.

assertions.description: Users can click 'Reject' on a pending skill to prevent it from being injected into prompts. The button has red styling (bg-red-500/10 text-red-600).
assertions.precondition: At least one skill with approval_status='pending' exists in user_skills with source='auto'
assertions.expected: After clicking, the skill disappears from the Pending tab. The Pending count decreases by 1 and the Rejected count increases by 1.

assertions.description: Users can click 'Reset to Pending' on an approved or rejected skill (in its expanded detail view) to return it to the pending state for re-review. The button has amber styling (bg-amber-500/10 text-amber-600).
assertions.precondition: A skill with approval_status='approved' or 'rejected' has been expanded by clicking its chevron
assertions.expected: After clicking, the skill moves to the Pending tab. The source status count decreases by 1 and the Pending count increases by 1.

assertions.description: Users can click any filter tab (Pending, Approved, Rejected, All) to switch which skills are displayed. The active tab gets primary styling (bg-primary text-primary-foreground) while inactive tabs show muted styling.
assertions.expected: Clicking switches the content area to show only skills matching the selected status. The clicked tab gets bg-primary styling. The count in parentheses reflects the actual number of skills in that category.

assertions.description: Users can click the chevron button on a skill row to toggle the detail panel open or closed

target.label: Chevron expand button on a skill row

assertions.precondition: At least one auto-extracted skill exists
assertions.expected: Clicking toggles the detail panel. Only one skill can be expanded at a time -- expanding a new skill collapses the previously expanded one. The chevron rotates from right-pointing to down-pointing.

groups.name: Loading, Error, and Refresh Behavior
groups.description: The panel fetches skills from GET /skills on mount (via useEffect) and on refresh button click. During fetch, the RefreshCw icon gains the animate-spin CSS class. If the API returns an error or the fetch throws, a red error message appears in the content area. The panel filters the API response client-side to only show skills with source='auto'.

assertions.description: Under normal operation, no error message is visible -- the page loads skills successfully from GET /skills
assertions.expected: No element with class text-destructive containing error text is visible. If this assertion fails, the GET /skills API endpoint is not responding.

assertions.description: Clicking the refresh button re-fetches skills from GET /skills and updates the displayed list. During fetch, the RefreshCw icon spins.
assertions.expected: After clicking, the icon briefly gains animate-spin class. When fetch completes, the skill list reflects the latest database state (including any newly extracted or modified skills).

assertions.description: When no skills match the active filter, users see a centered, muted text message instead of a blank area
assertions.expected: Pending filter shows: 'No pending skills to review. Skills are auto-extracted when workflows succeed after complex fixes.' Other filters show: 'No {status} skills found.'

groups.name: State Consistency After Mutations
groups.description: When a skill's approval status is changed, the filter tab counts must update immediately and the skill must appear under the correct filter. The state is managed client-side via React useState -- no page reload occurs. The API mutation (POST /skills/{id}/approve) fires before the state update, so a failed API call prevents the UI from changing.

assertions.description: The sum of Pending + Approved + Rejected counts always equals the total number of auto-extracted skills (visible on the All tab)
assertions.expected: Clicking 'All' shows every auto-extracted skill regardless of status. The total count should equal the sum of the three status counts shown on the other tabs.

assertions.description: After approving a skill, the Pending count decreases by 1 and the Approved count increases by 1, both immediately visible on the filter tabs
assertions.precondition: A pending skill was just approved by clicking its Approve button

assertions.description: After a skill is approved, it becomes eligible for injection into worker agent prompts during the agentic phase. The next workflow run's worker prompt will include a '## Procedural Skills (Auto-Learned)' section listing the approved skill's name, slug, category, and first sentence of description.
assertions.notes: This is a backend behavior -- not directly observable in the UI. The prompt injection is handled by build_skill_context() in integration.rs which queries WHERE approval_status = 'approved' AND source = 'auto'.

assertions.description: If the self-repair system auto-disables a skill (reverts from approved to pending after 3 consecutive failures), clicking Refresh shows the skill back in the Pending tab
assertions.precondition: An approved skill was auto-disabled by the self-repair system (3+ consecutive verification failures in a task run with the skill active), and the user clicked Refresh

groups.name: Visual Design and Layout
groups.description: The panel uses a vertical flex layout (flex-col h-full): header bar with border-b, filter tab bar with border-b, and flex-1 overflow-y-auto content area. Skill rows have border-b with last:border-0. Action buttons use 10px font size with semi-transparent colored backgrounds. Status icons are 14px (w-3.5 h-3.5). The expanded detail panel is indented to pl-10 to align with the skill name.

assertions.description: The header bar has a bottom border separating it from the filter tabs
assertions.expected: The header div has classes 'border-b border-border' providing visual separation from the filter tabs below

assertions.description: The currently active filter tab is visually distinguished from inactive tabs
assertions.expected: Active tab has classes 'bg-primary text-primary-foreground'. Inactive tabs have 'text-muted-foreground hover:bg-accent'. All tabs use 'text-xs rounded-md transition-colors'.

states.name: Loading State
states.description: Initial state while fetching skills from GET /skills on mount. The RefreshCw icon in the header has the animate-spin class. No skill rows or empty-state message are visible yet.

transitions.name: Load completes with no auto skills
transitions.description: The API returns successfully but no skills with source='auto' exist, showing the empty-state guidance message on the default Pending filter

transitions.name: Load completes with skills
transitions.description: The API returns auto-extracted skills that match the active filter, showing skill rows in the content area

states.name: Empty State — No Skills for Filter
states.description: No auto-extracted skills match the currently active filter tab. For the Pending filter (default), the message reads 'No pending skills to review. Skills are auto-extracted when workflows succeed after complex fixes.' For other filters it reads 'No {status} skills found.' The filter tab bar and refresh button remain visible.

transitions.name: Switch filter tab to one with skills
transitions.description: Click a different filter tab (Approved, Rejected, All) that has matching skills, transitioning to the list view

transitions.name: Switch filter tab to another empty filter
transitions.description: Click a different filter tab that also has no matching skills, staying in the empty state with an updated message

transitions.name: Refresh skills
transitions.description: Click the refresh button to re-fetch skills from GET /skills, returning to loading state

states.name: Skill List View
states.description: One or more auto-extracted skills are visible as collapsed rows in the content area. Each row shows a chevron toggle, a status icon (amber Clock for pending, green CheckCircle for approved, red XCircle for rejected), the skill name, and a metadata line. The filter tab bar shows counts for each status. Pending skills show inline Approve and Reject action buttons in the row.

transitions.name: Expand a skill row
transitions.description: Click the chevron on a skill row to expand it, revealing the detail panel with Description, Tags, Phases, Created, and Provenance fields

transitions.name: Approve a pending skill
transitions.description: Click the Approve button on a pending skill row. The skill immediately moves to the Approved filter tab, tab counts update, and the skill disappears from the Pending view. If this was the last pending skill, the view transitions to empty state.

transitions.name: Approve the last pending skill
transitions.description: Click Approve on the only remaining pending skill. After approval the Pending filter is empty, transitioning to the empty state.

transitions.name: Reject a pending skill
transitions.description: Click the Reject button on a pending skill row. The skill immediately moves to the Rejected filter tab and tab counts update.

transitions.name: Switch filter tab
transitions.description: Click a filter tab to show skills of a different status. If the target filter has skills, stays in list view; if empty, transitions to empty state.

transitions.name: Switch to empty filter tab
transitions.description: Click a filter tab that has no matching skills, transitioning to the empty state

transitions.name: Refresh skills
transitions.description: Click the refresh button to re-fetch skills from GET /skills

states.name: Skill Detail Expanded
states.description: A skill row is expanded, showing the detail panel below it. The panel is indented (pl-10) and contains labeled fields: Description, Tags, Phases, Created, and (for auto-extracted skills with provenance data) a Provenance section with Fix type, Source run, Fix ID, and Effectiveness. For approved/rejected skills, the expanded panel also shows Approve, Reject, and Reset to Pending action buttons.

transitions.name: Collapse skill detail
transitions.description: Click the expanded skill's chevron again to collapse the detail panel and return to the list view

transitions.name: Expand a different skill
transitions.description: Click a different skill row's chevron. The previously expanded skill collapses and the new one expands (only one expanded at a time).

transitions.name: Reset skill to pending
transitions.description: Click 'Reset to Pending' on an approved or rejected skill's expanded detail panel. The skill moves to the Pending tab and counts update.

transitions.name: Approve expanded skill
transitions.description: Click the Approve button in the expanded detail panel of an approved/rejected skill to change its status

transitions.name: Reject expanded skill
transitions.description: Click the Reject button in the expanded detail panel to reject the skill

transitions.name: Switch filter tab while expanded
transitions.description: Click a filter tab while a skill is expanded. The detail panel collapses and the list updates to show skills matching the new filter.

transitions.name: Refresh while expanded
transitions.description: Click the refresh button while a skill is expanded. All expansions collapse and data is re-fetched.
